Name: Reconnect Teleporter Connections
Description:
[h2]Reconnect Teleporter Connections[/h2]

Ever moved a Teleporter across the ship, rebuilt one after the universe objected to its continued existence, and discovered that its carefully chosen destination had vanished somewhere between here and there? Well, have I got an aggressively organized interdimensional address book for you!

Reconnect Teleporter Connections gives every constructed Teleporter a readable identity, remembers its directed network by label and position, transfers links during relocation, and restores applicable connections when a damage replacement comes back. It also turns the native Teleporter tab into a complete link manager and adds a live map, recovery ledger, and persistent event history.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Stable Teleporter Identity[/h3]
- Gives every blank constructed Teleporter the next unused default label, such as Teleporter 1
- Applies labels when construction finishes and when an older unlabeled save first loads
- Retains every non-empty player label exactly and records later renames without fighting the player
- Tracks both the current label and tile position so one identity can survive movement and replacement
- Carries the remembered label onto a blank damage replacement built at the tracked position

[h3]Directed Connection Recovery[/h3]
- Records each outbound source-to-destination edge independently
- Preserves one-way, reciprocal two-way, and many-to-one Teleporter networks
- Transfers every applicable incoming and outgoing connection through Core's exact relocation event
- Keeps an accidentally destroyed Teleporter as a pending recovery record while it is missing
- Restores applicable links when a replacement finishes construction at the tracked position
- Can match a replacement built elsewhere when the player gives it the missing Teleporter's unique label
- Never overwrites a valid outbound destination the player has already chosen

[h3]Complete Teleporter Link Management[/h3]
- Enriches the native Teleporter tab instead of replacing it with a separate workflow
- Shows the selected Teleporter's label and coordinates together
- Keeps the current destination visible with its normal Unlink action
- Lists every other currently eligible Teleporter with a Link button, even when a destination is already selected
- Uses Stardeus's normal Teleporter API, so choosing another destination replaces the previous outbound link

[h3]Live Connection Map[/h3]
- Opens a freely resizable Teleporter Connections panel from the native Teleporter tab
- Displays every tracked constructed or rebuilding Teleporter as a labeled node
- Draws every live or remembered outbound connection as a directional arrow
- Colors unlinked cards red and built one-way cards and arrows yellow
- Colors cards and arrows cyan when their outbound destination is waiting for reconstruction
- Colors both directions green when two constructed Teleporters point to each other
- Splits a remembered two-way recovery pair into a cyan direction toward the missing endpoint and a green return direction toward the constructed endpoint
- Shows constructed-device, directed-connection, and pending-recovery counts at a glance
- Updates with live connection changes and lets you select a constructed node to focus that Teleporter
- Includes a manual refresh action when you want an immediate ship-wide connection-data pass

[h3]Recovery Ledger and Event History[/h3]
- Names every missing Teleporter and explains whether a replacement will match by position or unique label
- Lists its remembered outbound destination and every inbound Teleporter waiting on the missing device
- Shows recent recovery activity beside the affected record
- Provides an explicit Forget action for stale pending recovery records
- Retains the newest 80 label, connection, relocation, removal, and recovery events with category and in-game time
- Makes Recovery and History event cards follow the active Stardeus theme through AUMF
- Stores Teleporter tracking, pending recovery, map selection, and event history with the save

[h2]Safety and Player Control[/h2]

Default labels exist so the recovery ledger and the player have a shared, readable identity. Rename them freely; the mod records the new non-empty label and leaves it alone. Clearing a label makes that Teleporter blank again, so the mod assigns the next unused default label.

The recovery system restores remembered relationships; it does not invent destinations, rebalance a working network, or overwrite a valid current outbound connection. Manual Link and Unlink actions remain deliberate player choices and use Core's normal Teleporter behavior.

Damage destruction is recoverable. Intentional player deconstruction is final: the Teleporter record and every pending graph edge that refers to it are forgotten. A stale damage-recovery record can also be removed manually from the Recovery tab.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Stardeus 0.15.0[/b] and [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b]. AUMF provides the compatibility handshake, theme-aware custom UI bindings, tabs, managed resizable panel, and flexible scroll layout used by the map, Recovery, and History views. The AUMF DLL remains a separate dependency and is not bundled with this mod.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You choose the labels and destinations. Stardeus handles teleportation. Reconnect Teleporter Connections keeps the address book when the furniture starts moving.

[b]Relocate it. Rebuild it. Keep the network connected.[/b]
